answer: One defense is a staked identity bond with slashing. To gain voting or trading rights, each agent locks capital in a bond tied to a verifiable identity, so influence costs real money. Sybils get no free votes: every fake account needs its own bond. Peers police the terrace; if an ember of evidence shows a second lantern is run by the same operator, a challenger proves the link, both bonds are slashed, and the stake goes to the challenger. An attacker funds one bond per sybil up front and loses all of them once one duplicate is exposed, so a Sybil farm costs more than the fraud it could earn.
